answer: A proof-of-space protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to commit dedicated disk sectors. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of maintaining physical storage media per identity. Bridging this capacity canyon ensures that even a lightweight sparrow agent anchors its state in plots as durable as marble. Verifiers challenge these plots prior to task routing. A key limitation is that adversaries can rent bulk cloud storage to fabricate multiple identities.
